intro.say: Something is symmetrical when both halves match, like a butterfly's wings!

rounds.say: Fold a butterfly down the middle. The left wing and the right wing match exactly!
rounds.caption: both sides match

rounds.say: A heart is symmetrical too. Draw a line down the middle, and the two halves are the same.
rounds.caption: fold down the middle

options.label: snail
options.why: The snail's shell is only on one side.

options.label: key
options.why: A key's teeth are only on one side.

rounds.explain: A butterfly's two wings match, so it is symmetrical.

options.why: One eye is winking, so the sides don't match.
One eyebrow is up, so the sides don't match.

rounds.explain: The smiley face has the same eye on each side, so both halves match.

rounds.ask: Fold this heart in half. Will the two halves match?

options.label: No
options.why: Look again: both sides of a heart are the same.

rounds.explain: Both halves of a heart are the same shape, so they match.

options.label: star
options.why: A star matches when you fold it down the middle.

options.label: heart
options.why: A heart's halves match.

rounds.explain: A key has teeth on just one side, so its halves don't match.

rounds.ask: Do both halves match? Sort them!
rounds.explain: A heart, star and flower match on both sides. A key, snail and boot don't.

intro.say: A line of symmetry is a fold line where both halves match. Even letters can have one!

rounds.say: The letter A has a line of symmetry straight down the middle. The left side matches the right side.
rounds.caption: A · fold down the middle

rounds.say: The letter B has a line going across the middle. The top half matches the bottom half!
rounds.caption: B · fold across

rounds.ask: Which letter matches on both sides when you fold it down the middle?

options.label: R
options.why: R's leg sticks out on one side.

options.label: F
options.why: F's arms only point one way.

rounds.explain: T has the same arm on each side of the middle line.

options.label: M
options.why: M matches down the middle.

options.label: H
options.why: H matches down the middle.

rounds.explain: L has its foot on only one side, so the halves don't match.

rounds.ask: Sort the letters. Are they symmetrical?
rounds.explain: A, O and H have matching halves. F, J and R don't.

options.why: The two ends are different colours.
The two ends are different colours.

rounds.explain: Red, blue, red is the same from both ends, so it matches in the middle.

rounds.ask: Which number matches on both sides when folded down the middle?

options.why: The top of a 7 points one way.
A 2 curves one way and not the other.

rounds.explain: An 8 has two matching halves, left and right.

intro.say: Let's be mirror makers! We'll finish patterns so both halves match.

rounds.say: In a mirror pattern, the right side copies the left side backwards, like a reflection.
Words can be symmetrical too! M, O and M each match on both sides, so MOM looks the same in a mirror.
rounds.caption: MOM

rounds.ask: Finish the mirror. What goes in the gap?

options.why: The banana is already next to the mirror line.
There are no grapes on the left side.

rounds.explain: The apple is on the far left, so it must be on the far right too.

rounds.ask: Finish the mirror. What goes in the gap?

options.why: Red is next to the mirror line already.
Blue is at the very end.

rounds.explain: Green is second from the left, so it is second from the right too.
rounds.hint: Count out from the mirror line.

rounds.ask: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?

options.why: Try folding it more than one way.
Don't forget the corner to corner folds.

rounds.explain: Fold it up and down, side to side, and along both corner to corner lines: 4 ways!

rounds.ask: Which shape has the MOST lines of symmetry?

options.why: A triangle has 3 at most.
A square has 4. One shape has even more.

rounds.explain: A circle matches when you fold it through the middle any way at all!

rounds.ask: Which word looks the same in a mirror?

options.label: SUN
options.why: S and N are not symmetrical.

options.label: DOG
options.why: D and G are not symmetrical down the middle.

rounds.explain: W, O and W each match on both sides, and the word reads the same both ways.

rounds.ask: A butterfly has 3 spots on its left wing. Its wings are symmetrical. How many spots in all?

options.why: The right wing has spots too.
Both wings match, so each has 3.

rounds.explain: The right wing matches with 3 spots, and 3 and 3 make 6.
